heart_intro_scene1_overview.display_text: Welcome! In this lab you’ll explore the human heart from two angles—an intact exterior view and a cutaway interior view. Keep in mind: right and left are defined from the patient’s perspective.
heart_intro_scene1_overview.llm_text: Welcome! In this lab you’ll explore the human heart from two angles—an intact exterior view and a cutaway interior view. Keep in mind: right and left are defined from the patient’s perspective.
heart_intro_scene1_overview.spoken_text: Welcome! In this lab you’ll explore the human heart from two angles—an intact exterior view and a cutaway interior view. Keep in mind: right and left are defined from the patient’s perspective.

heart_scene1_gross_orientation_rotation.display_text: Notice the apex points down and slightly to the left. As you rotate, always remember we’re describing structures from the patient’s own right/left.
heart_scene1_gross_orientation_rotation.llm_text: Notice the apex points down and slightly to the left. As you rotate, always remember we’re describing structures from the patient’s own right/left.
heart_scene1_gross_orientation_rotation.spoken_text: Notice the apex points down and slightly to the left. As you rotate, always remember we’re describing structures from the patient’s own right/left.

heart_scene1_major_vessels_intro.display_text: On the exterior heart, track the vena cavae, pulmonary trunk/arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta. In the cutaway view, those connections lead you to chambers and valves inside.
heart_scene1_major_vessels_intro.llm_text: On the exterior heart, track the vena cavae, pulmonary trunk or arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta. In the cutaway view, those connections lead you to chambers and valves inside.
heart_scene1_major_vessels_intro.spoken_text: On the exterior heart, track the vena cavae, pulmonary trunk or arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta. In the cutaway view, those connections lead you to chambers and valves inside.

heart_scene2_tour_chambers_intro.display_text: Let’s tour the heart interior. We’ll go chamber by chamber, then valves, then the major vessels that connect to each side.
heart_scene2_tour_chambers_intro.llm_text: Let’s tour the heart interior. We’ll go chamber by chamber, then valves, then the major vessels that connect to each side.
heart_scene2_tour_chambers_intro.spoken_text: Let’s tour the heart interior. We’ll go chamber by chamber, then valves, then the major vessels that connect to each side.

heart_scene2_highlight_right_atrium.display_text: Right atrium receives blood coming back from the body.
heart_scene2_highlight_right_atrium.llm_text: Right atrium receives blood coming back from the body.
heart_scene2_highlight_right_atrium.spoken_text: Right atrium receives blood coming back from the body.

heart_scene2_highlight_right_ventricle.display_text: Right ventricle pumps forward toward the pulmonary circuit.
heart_scene2_highlight_right_ventricle.llm_text: Right ventricle pumps forward toward the pulmonary circuit.
heart_scene2_highlight_right_ventricle.spoken_text: Right ventricle pumps forward toward the pulmonary circuit.

heart_scene2_highlight_left_atrium.display_text: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood via the pulmonary veins.
heart_scene2_highlight_left_atrium.llm_text: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood via the pulmonary veins.
heart_scene2_highlight_left_atrium.spoken_text: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood via the pulmonary veins.

heart_scene2_highlight_left_ventricle.display_text: Left ventricle is the powerful chamber that drives blood to the entire body.
heart_scene2_highlight_left_ventricle.llm_text: Left ventricle is the powerful chamber that drives blood to the entire body.
heart_scene2_highlight_left_ventricle.spoken_text: Left ventricle is the powerful chamber that drives blood to the entire body.

heart_scene2_highlight_tricuspid_valve.display_text: Tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle into the right atrium.
heart_scene2_highlight_tricuspid_valve.llm_text: Tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle into the right atrium.
heart_scene2_highlight_tricuspid_valve.spoken_text: Tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle into the right atrium.

heart_scene2_highlight_pulmonary_valve.display_text: Pulmonary (pulmonic) valve directs flow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
heart_scene2_highlight_pulmonary_valve.llm_text: Pulmonary (pulmonic) valve directs flow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
heart_scene2_highlight_pulmonary_valve.spoken_text: Pulmonary (pulmonic) valve directs flow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.

heart_scene2_highlight_mitral_bicuspid_v.display_text: This valve is called the mitral valve or the bicuspid valve—same structure between the left atrium and left ventricle.
heart_scene2_highlight_mitral_bicuspid_v.llm_text: This valve is called the mitral valve or the bicuspid valve—same structure between the left atrium and left ventricle.
heart_scene2_highlight_mitral_bicuspid_v.spoken_text: This valve is called the mitral valve or the bicuspid valve—same structure between the left atrium and left ventricle.

heart_scene2_highlight_aortic_valve.display_text: Aortic valve prevents blood from flowing back into the left ventricle.
heart_scene2_highlight_aortic_valve.llm_text: Aortic valve prevents blood from flowing back into the left ventricle.
heart_scene2_highlight_aortic_valve.spoken_text: Aortic valve prevents blood from flowing back into the left ventricle.

heart_scene2_highlight_vessels_sequence.display_text: Now focus on the major vessels: superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta.
heart_scene2_highlight_vessels_sequence.llm_text: Now focus on the major vessels: superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta.
heart_scene2_highlight_vessels_sequence.spoken_text: Now focus on the major vessels: superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and the aorta.

heart_scene3_dual_circuit_intro.display_text: Here’s dual circulation. Blue represents deoxygenated blood moving through the right side and toward the lungs. Red represents oxygenated blood moving through the left side and toward the body.
heart_scene3_dual_circuit_intro.llm_text: Here’s dual circulation. Blue represents deoxygenated blood moving through the right side and toward the lungs. Red represents oxygenated blood moving through the left side and toward the body.
heart_scene3_dual_circuit_intro.spoken_text: Here’s dual circulation. Blue represents deoxygenated blood moving through the right side and toward the lungs. Red represents oxygenated blood moving through the left side and toward the body.

heart_scene3_pulmonary_focus_highlight.display_text: First, pulmonary circulation: blood leaves the right ventricle, travels to the lungs, and returns oxygenated back toward the left atrium.
heart_scene3_pulmonary_focus_highlight.llm_text: First, pulmonary circulation: blood leaves the right ventricle, travels to the lungs, and returns oxygenated back toward the left atrium.
heart_scene3_pulmonary_focus_highlight.spoken_text: First, pulmonary circulation: blood leaves the right ventricle, travels to the lungs, and returns oxygenated back toward the left atrium.

heart_scene3_systemic_focus_highlight.display_text: Now systemic circulation: oxygenated blood exits the left ventricle through the aortic valve and delivers oxygen to the entire body—then returns deoxygenated to the right side.
heart_scene3_systemic_focus_highlight.llm_text: Now systemic circulation: oxygenated blood exits the left ventricle through the aortic valve and delivers oxygen to the entire body—then returns deoxygenated to the right side.
heart_scene3_systemic_focus_highlight.spoken_text: Now systemic circulation: oxygenated blood exits the left ventricle through the aortic valve and delivers oxygen to the entire body—then returns deoxygenated to the right side.

heart_scene3_steady_state_summary.display_text: In steady state, the two loops are linked: the heart continuously alternates pressure and flow direction through pulmonary and systemic circuits.
heart_scene3_steady_state_summary.llm_text: In steady state, the two loops are linked: the heart continuously alternates pressure and flow direction through pulmonary and systemic circuits.
heart_scene3_steady_state_summary.spoken_text: In steady state, the two loops are linked: the heart continuously alternates pressure and flow direction through pulmonary and systemic circuits.

heart_scene4_trace_intro.display_text: Press Next to advance the blood cell one step along the circulation pathway. Watch the label and color changes closely.
heart_scene4_trace_intro.llm_text: Press next to advance the blood cell one step along the circulation pathway. Watch the label and color changes closely.
heart_scene4_trace_intro.spoken_text: Press next to advance the blood cell one step along the circulation pathway. Watch the label and color changes closely.

heart_scene4_step_RA_to_tricuspid_to_RV.display_text: The right atrium contracts, pushing blood through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
heart_scene4_step_RA_to_tricuspid_to_RV.llm_text: The right atrium contracts, pushing blood through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
heart_scene4_step_RA_to_tricuspid_to_RV.spoken_text: The right atrium contracts, pushing blood through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.

heart_scene4_step_RV_to_pulmonary_valve_.display_text: The right ventricle contracts, pushing blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
heart_scene4_step_RV_to_pulmonary_valve_.llm_text: The right ventricle contracts, pushing blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
heart_scene4_step_RV_to_pulmonary_valve_.spoken_text: The right ventricle contracts, pushing blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.

heart_scene4_step_pulmonary_arteries_to_.display_text: In the lung capillaries, the cell picks up oxygen—so it turns from blue to red.
heart_scene4_step_pulmonary_arteries_to_.llm_text: In the lung capillaries, the cell picks up oxygen—so it turns from blue to red.
heart_scene4_step_pulmonary_arteries_to_.spoken_text: In the lung capillaries, the cell picks up oxygen—so it turns from blue to red.

heart_scene4_step_lungs_to_left_atrium_t.display_text: Oxygenated blood returns through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium, then flows through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.
heart_scene4_step_lungs_to_left_atrium_t.llm_text: Oxygenated blood returns through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium, then flows through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.
heart_scene4_step_lungs_to_left_atrium_t.spoken_text: Oxygenated blood returns through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium, then flows through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.

heart_scene4_step_LV_to_aortic_valve_to_.display_text: The left ventricle contracts, sending blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.
heart_scene4_step_LV_to_aortic_valve_to_.llm_text: The left ventricle contracts, sending blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.
heart_scene4_step_LV_to_aortic_valve_to_.spoken_text: The left ventricle contracts, sending blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.

heart_scene4_step_systemic_return_to_SVC.display_text: After oxygen is delivered to the body, the blood returns through systemic veins into the vena cavae and back to the right atrium. That completes the loop.
heart_scene4_step_systemic_return_to_SVC.llm_text: After oxygen is delivered to the body, the blood returns through systemic veins into the vena cavae and back to the right atrium. That completes the loop.
heart_scene4_step_systemic_return_to_SVC.spoken_text: After oxygen is delivered to the body, the blood returns through systemic veins into the vena cavae and back to the right atrium. That completes the loop.
